chunks: And Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Sa'd ibn Abi Khalaf, from Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) who said:

"The obligatory prayers, at their first time, when their limits are established, are more fragrant than a shoot of the aspen tree when it is taken from its tree in its fragrance, scent, and freshness. So be upon the first time."

key_terms.قَضِيبُ الْآسِ: A shoot of the aspen tree

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit of performing obligatory prayers at their first time according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam Musa al-Kazim (peace be upon him), the virtue of offering obligatory prayers at their earliest time (al-waqt al-awwal) is highlighted through a vivid sensory metaphor, comparing the spiritual fragrance of such prayers to that of a fresh, tender shoot of the aspen tree. This emphasizes not merely punctuality, but the excellence of hastening to worship while the heart is still fresh and the command is immediate, a concept deeply valued in Shia fiqh for maximizing reward and demonstrating eagerness to obey God.
